title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 191
paragraphs: West of the river Triton, next after the Auseans, come Libyans who are tillers of the soil and whose custom it is to have fixed dwellings; they are called the Maxyes. They grow their hair long on the right side of the head and cut it short on the left, and they smear their bodies with red ochre. They claim to be descended from the men who came from Troy.

This country and the rest of Libya toward the west are both much more frequented by wild beasts and far more thickly wooded than the country of the nomads. Whereas the eastern part of Libya, where the nomads live, is low-lying and sandy up to the river Triton, what lies west of it—the country of the tillers—is very mountainous, densely wooded, and full of wild beasts. For in the land of these people are found the monstrous serpent, the lion, the elephant, bears, venomous snakes, horned asses, and also the dog-headed men and the headless men with eyes in their chests—at least so say the Libyans about them—and the wild men and wild women, and a great multitude of other beasts that are not fabulous like these.
